I have two offers and I cannot decide.
Two? That is a good problem. Which one pays more?
The bank. Six hundred more. But it is located fifty minutes away.
Fifty each way? That is worse than my distance.
The other one is remote and the schedule is much more flexible.
So the second one is more convenient. But is the experience as good?
Honestly? Better. The team is smaller, so I would do more.
Then why are we talking about this?
Because the salary is lower and my mother keeps saying the bank looks better on a resume.
Your mother is not going to commute fifty minutes twice a day.
The startup is more flexible than the bank.
The salary is lower, but the experience is better.
It is not as convenient as the other one.
For me, that is the most important thing.
I see your point, but I still think this one is better.

Right, so I chose. And it was harder than I expected. The first one paid four hundred reais more, which is a lot when you are a student, and the office is beautiful. But it is fifty minutes away and the schedule is completely fixed. The second one is remote two days a week, so I save four hours, and the team is much smaller. In the end that is what decided it. Six people instead of forty. I am going to do real work, not photocopies. The salary is worse, but I think I am going to learn more. Ask me again in three months.

Good morning. Two internship programmes are open, and students keep asking me which is better, so here are the facts. The first is three months, starts in March, and it is the most competitive one we have: twelve places, and about four hundred students apply. The second is longer, six months, starting in April, and it is less competitive, but the hours are also less flexible. Both require advanced English and both require third semester or above. Neither is better. They are different. Choose the one that fits your schedule, not the one with the bigger name.
